Heard on I.A. No.03/2024 (filed in CRA No.959/2024) and I.A. No.1/2024 (filed in CRA No.1076/2024), which are applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants in these appeals.

By the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07-05-2024 passed by the learned Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Rajnandgaon in Special (Atrocities)
Session Case No. 23/2021, appellant Jagdish Kumar has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 366 and 370 IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 7-7 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- Rs.5000/-, in default of payment of fine to further undergo RI for 2-2 months respectively, whereas, appellant Maneesh Sharma has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 370 and 376 IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 7-7 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- Rs.5000/-, in default of payment of fine to further undergo RI for 2-2 months respectively, with a direction that all the jail sentences shall run concurrently.

sentences.text: Prosecution case in brief is that the husband of the victim was suffering from fracture in his hand and to look after him and her three children, she used to do work as labourer.

It is alleged that during that period, the victim came in contact with co-accused Lakshmi Bai who used to do the work of cleaning utensils in the marriage functions and she offered her to go outside the state for earning and stay along with her.

On 12-02-2021, the victim received a phone call from co-accused Lakshmi Bai in the evening at about 4:00-5:00 pm to meet her and she she met with co-accused Lakshmi Bai,
she asked the victim to go along with the co-accused Salim Mohammad in a motor cycle to her house and therefore, she went there stayed in the house of co- accused Lakshmi Bai for the night and on 14-02-2021 at about 4.00 am, the appellant Jagdish Kumar and co-accused Salim Mohammad came in a car and they took the victim to district Nagaur,
Rajasthan where appellant Jagdish Kumar introduced her to appellant Maneesh Sharma and asked the victim to marry with said Maneesh Sharma.
The allegation against the present appellants are that they conspired with co-accused Lakshmi Bai and Salim Mohammad in transportation and trafficking of the victim which is prima facie apparent.

When she refused to marry, co-accused Lakshmi Bai informed that she has been sold to appellant Maneesh Sharma for Rs. 2,00,000/- and thereafter she was forcefully taken to the notary office where the name of her husband has been changed to father's name mentioning as Bhagat Diwakar and fake aadhar card was prepared and her marriage was performed with appellant Maneesh Sharma.
Thereafter the victim was taken to village Bhakri, PS Pilwa, District Nagaur, Rajasthan and she was threatened and sexually exploited.

When husband of the victim did not receive any information from her, he lodged a missing report at police station Tumdibode and on being searched by the police, she was recovered from the custody of the appellant Maneesh Sharma at village Bhakri, PS Pilwa, District Nagaur.
It has been argued by counsel for appellant Jagdish Kumar that he is not in contact with the other co-accused persons and he has been falsely implicated in the offence.
In her evidence the victim stated that she herself left her house and went to Rajasthan to earn her livelihood.
He has not assisted co-accused persons in performing marriage with other co-accused Maneesh Sharma.
The appellant is in jail since 16-06-2021 and final adjudication of the appeal will take its own time.
Therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.
It is argued by learned counsel for appellant Maneesh Sharma that the victim herself had come to his village at Rajasthan and on her own will he performed marriage with her.

Subsequently, a false allegation of purchase of the victim has been developed by the other co-accused persons to extort money from him and thereby this appellant has been falsely implicated in the offence.
Appellant Maneesh Sharma is also in jail since 31-03-2021 and final adjudication of the case will take its own time.
Therefore, he may be enlarge on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the applications and submits that there seems to be prima facie case against the present appellants as to their involvement in offence in question.
He also submits that bail application of co-accused Salim Mohammad has already been rejected vide order dated 13-08-2024 passed in CRA No.961/2024.
Therefore, present appellants are not entitled for grant of bail.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the trial Court.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, evidence led by the prosecution, the nature of evidence and allegations against the appellants, the severity of the offence, I am not inclined to allow the applications filed by these appellants for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.03/2024 filed in CRA No.959/2024 and I.A. No.1/2024 filed in CRA No.1076/2024, applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail are rejected.
List these appeals for final hearing along with CRA No.961/2024 after eight weeks.
